title: Detect an uncertainty floor that more same-sensor observations cannot remove
statement: One common sensor bias b can remain a shared polyhedral variable and be eliminated by exact Fourier-Motzkin projection. For Fb(x)=4x-b and sensor+b, every adaptive report is4x for b in[-1/2,1/2]. Future gains2 and1 give contrast p1/2-p2/3+b/6, forcing a worst-case radius>=1/12 even after arbitrarily many same-sensor readings.

requires: One shared scalar source across all modules and times, independently warranted global constants and sensor-error contract; affine virtual evaluation expressions. Mixed inverse gains m-K_j>a, or the stated scalar network contraction m>a*||L||infinity. The order-only branch instead supplies stationarity, continuity and monotonicity with K<m.

assumptions: No automatic vector-valued noisy completion, general mixed-feedback LP or inference of global physical regularity from finite readings. Quantitative Lipschitz and qualitative monotone contracts are different. Missing five programs/results/clean replay archive means task radii, speed and execution identity remain source reports. Correlation-aware representation did not improve four negative-control tasks. Equally informed ordinary retaining methods can tie.
costs: Pay historical readings, source-aware task/reference checks, shared calibration, stored constraints, factorial order enumeration and rational arithmetic. Zero new later learner calls is not free acquisition. Reported133380/22230 intersections are source calculations, not a complexity ceiling. External exact calibration is a separate paid instrument privilege.
contract.units: Source-local energy/time/amplitude and dimensionless probability/radius conventions; no automatic physical conversion.
contract.obstruction: Warrant source identity/regularity/calibration physically and acquire current programs/results before treating reported numerical reductions as replayed. Preserve genuine unattained order endpoints and exact-versus-outer domain boundaries.

body: The source/instrument pair is observationally identical at every possible input, so adaptation cannot distinguish it. Physical responses differ by the explicit affine b term. A separately exact-calibrated sensor is a new paid interface. Retaining a common bias can tighten bounds relative to independent inflation but does not resolve the gauge; four source-reported negative-control tasks had no improvement. Do not infer a generally superior learner or free calibration from this mathematical mechanism.
